verses.text: Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the days of adversity come and the years approach of which you will say, “I find no pleasure in them,”

xrefs.text: It is good for a man to bear the yoke while he is still young.
So if a man lives many years, let him rejoice in them all. But let him remember the days of darkness, for they will be many. Everything to come is futile.
O God, You have taught me from my youth, and to this day I proclaim Your marvelous deeds.
Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it.
But Jesus called the children to Him and said, “Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them! For the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.

verses.text: before the light of the sun, moon, and stars is darkened, and the clouds return after the rain,

xrefs.text: In that day they will roar over it, like the roaring of the sea. If one looks over the land, he will see darkness and distress; even the light will be obscured by clouds.
As soon as the ark of God was mentioned, Eli fell backward from his chair by the city gate, and being old and heavy, he broke his neck and died. And Eli had judged Israel forty years.
And at that time Eli, whose eyesight had grown so dim that he could not see, was lying in his room.
Now Eli was ninety-eight years old, and his gaze was fixed because he could not see.
Now Israel’s eyesight was poor because of old age; he could hardly see. Joseph brought his sons to him, and his father kissed them and embraced them.

verses.text: on the day the keepers of the house tremble and the strong men stoop, when those grinding cease because they are few and those watching through windows see dimly,

xrefs.text: For all our days decline in Your fury; we finish our years with a sigh.
He has broken my strength on the way; He has cut short my days.
Now Israel’s eyesight was poor because of old age; he could hardly see. Joseph brought his sons to him, and his father kissed them and embraced them.
This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Old men and old women will again sit along the streets of Jerusalem, each with a staff in hand because of great age.
Once again the Philistines waged war against Israel, and David and his servants went down and fought against the Philistines. But David became exhausted.

verses.text: when the doors to the street are shut and the sound of the mill fades away, when one rises at the sound of a bird and all the daughters of song grow faint,

xrefs.text: Moreover, I will banish from them the sounds of joy and gladness, the voices of the bride and bridegroom, the sound of the millstones, and the light of the lamp.

I am now eighty years old. Can I discern what is good and what is not? Can your servant taste what he eats or drinks? Can I still hear the voice of singing men and women? Why should your servant be an added burden to my lord the king?

And the sound of harpists and musicians, of flute players and trumpeters, will never ring out in you again. Nor will any craftsmen of any trade be found in you again, nor the sound of a millstone be heard in you again.

verses.text: when men fear the heights and dangers of the road, when the almond tree blossoms, the grasshopper loses its spring, and the caper berry shrivels— for then man goes to his eternal home and mourners walk the streets.

xrefs.text: If I look for Sheol as my home, if I spread out my bed in darkness,
Yes, I know that You will bring me down to death, to the place appointed for all the living.
This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Take note, and summon the wailing women; send for the most skillful among them.
Gray hair is a crown of glory; it is attained along the path of righteousness.
Both the gray-haired and the aged are on our side— men much older than your father.

verses.text: Remember Him before the silver cord is snapped and the golden bowl is crushed, before the pitcher is shattered at the spring and the wheel is broken at the well,

xrefs.text: “What do you see?” he asked. “I see a solid gold lampstand,” I replied, “with a bowl at the top and seven lamps on it, with seven spouts to the lamps.

verses.text: before the dust returns to the ground from which it came and the spirit returns to God who gave it.

xrefs.text: And many who sleep in the dust of the earth will awake, some to everlasting life, but others to shame and everlasting contempt.
All go to one place; all come from dust, and all return to dust.
When his spirit departs, he returns to the ground; on that very day his plans perish.
By the sweat of your brow you will eat your bread, until you return to the ground— because out of it were you taken. For dust you are, and to dust you shall return.”
If He were to set His heart to it and withdraw His Spirit and breath,

verses.text: “Futility of futilities,” says the Teacher. “Everything is futile!”

xrefs.text: “Futility of futilities,” says the Teacher, “futility of futilities! Everything is futile!”
As no man has power over the wind to contain it, so no one has authority over his day of death. As no one can be discharged in wartime, so wickedness will not release those who practice it.
For who knows what is good for a man during the few days in which he passes through his fleeting life like a shadow? Who can tell a man what will come after him under the sun?
So I hated life, because the work that is done under the sun was grievous to me. For everything is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
I saw that all labor and success spring from a man’s envy of his neighbor. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.

verses.text: Not only was the Teacher wise, but he also taught the people knowledge; he pondered, searched out, and arranged many proverbs.

xrefs.text: Solomon composed three thousand proverbs, and his songs numbered a thousand and five.
These are the proverbs of Solomon son of David, king of Israel,
These are additional proverbs of Solomon, which were copied by the men of Hezekiah king of Judah:
How blessed are your men! How blessed are these servants of yours who stand continually before you and hear your wisdom!
The proverbs of Solomon: A wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish son grief to his mother.

verses.text: The Teacher searched to find delightful sayings and to record accurate words of truth.

xrefs.text: the faith and love proceeding from the hope stored up for you in heaven, of which you have already heard in the word of truth, the gospel
This is a trustworthy saying, worthy of full acceptance: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am the worst.
The wise in heart are called discerning, and pleasant speech promotes instruction.
These are the proverbs of Solomon son of David, king of Israel,
Incline your ear and hear the words of the wise— apply your mind to my knowledge—

verses.text: The words of the wise are like goads, and the anthologies of the masters are like firmly embedded nails driven by a single Shepherd.

xrefs.text: For the word of God is living and active. Sharper than any double-edged sword, it pierces even to dividing soul and spirit, joints and marrow. It judges the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
“Is not My word like fire,” declares the LORD, “and like a hammer that smashes a rock?”
When the people heard this, they were cut to the heart and asked Peter and the other apostles, “Brothers, what shall we do?
I will appoint over them one shepherd, My servant David, and he will feed them. He will feed them and be their shepherd.
The weapons of our warfare are not the weapons of the flesh. Instead, they have divine power to demolish strongholds.

verses.text: And by these, my son, be further warned: There is no end to the making of many books, and much study wearies the body.

xrefs.text: For with much wisdom comes much sorrow, and as knowledge grows, grief increases.
There are many more things that Jesus did. If all of them were written down, I suppose that not even the world itself would have space for the books that would be written.
You pore over the Scriptures because you presume that by them you possess eternal life. These are the very words that testify about Me,

We also have the word of the prophets as confirmed beyond doubt. And you will do well to pay attention to it, as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts.
But Abraham replied, ‘They have Moses and the Prophets; let your brothers listen to them.

verses.text: When all has been heard, the conclusion of the matter is this: Fear God and keep His commandments, because this is the whole duty of man.

xrefs.text: And now, O Israel, what does the LORD your God ask of you but to fear the LORD your God by walking in all His ways, to love Him, to serve the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul,
He has shown you, O man, what is good. And what does the LORD require of you but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?

so that you and your children and grandchildren may fear the LORD your God all the days of your lives by keeping all His statutes and commandments that I give you, and so that your days may be prolonged.
The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom; all who follow His precepts gain rich understanding. His praise endures forever!
He fulfills the desires of those who fear Him; He hears their cry and saves them.

verses.text: For God will bring every deed into judgment, along with every hidden thing, whether good or evil.

xrefs.text: For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that each one may receive his due for the things done in the body, whether good or bad.
on the day when God will judge men’s secrets through Christ Jesus, as proclaimed by my gospel.
But I tell you that men will give an account on the day of judgment for every careless word they have spoken.

Therefore judge nothing before the appointed time; wait until the Lord comes. He will bring to light what is hidden in darkness and will expose the motives of men’s hearts. At that time each will receive his praise from God.
So do not be afraid of them. For there is nothing concealed that will not be disclosed, and nothing hidden that will not be made known.
